HLSHFO

This product covers the Hawaiian islands

**LALA REMAINS A HURRICANE AS IT CONTINUES NORTHWESTWARD ON THE
LEEWARD SIDE OF THE BIG ISLAND**

NEW INFORMATION
---------------

* CHANGES TO WATCHES AND WARNINGS:
- None

* CURRENT WATCHES AND WARNINGS:
- A Hurricane Warning is in effect for Big Island East, Big
Island Interior, Big Island North, Big Island South, Big Island
Southeast, Big Island Summits, Kohala, and Kona
- A Tropical Storm Warning is in effect for Central Oahu, East
Honolulu, Ewa Plain, Haleakala Summit, Honolulu Metro,
Kahoolawe, Kauai East, Kauai Mountains, Kauai North, Kauai
South, Kauai Southwest, Kipahulu, Koolau Leeward, Koolau
Windward, Lanai Leeward, Lanai Mauka, Lanai South, Lanai
Windward, Maui Central Valley North, Maui Central Valley South,
Maui Leeward West, Maui Windward West, Molokai Leeward South,
Molokai North, Molokai Southeast, Molokai West, Molokai
Windward, Niihau, Oahu North Shore, Olomana, South Haleakala,
South Maui/Upcountry, Waianae Coast, Waianae Mountains, and
Windward Haleakala

* STORM INFORMATION:
- About 180 miles south-southeast of Honolulu or about 50 miles
south-southwest of Kailua-Kona
- 19.1N 156.5W
- Storm Intensity 75 mph
- Movement Northwest or 310 degrees at 10 mph

SITUATION OVERVIEW
------------------

Hurricane Lala continues to bring damaging winds, heavy rainfall
leading to flash flooding, and dangerously high surf to portions of
the state. Heavy rain associated with the hurricane extends across the
Big Island and Maui County this evening and will spread northwest to
reach Oahu tonight and Kauai late tonight into Sunday morning.
Hurricane Lala passed south of the Big Island this afternoon and will
continue generally west-northwestward, tracking south of the island
chain through Sunday. Do not focus on the exact forecast track or
intensity of Lala as impacts extend well beyond the center of the
hurricane.

Rainfall between 10 to 17 inches has been observed over the last
12 hours for the eastern Big Island. Up to 9 inches of rain has been
measured on eastern Maui over the last 12 hours. Flooding rain will
continue for portions of the Big Island of Hawaii as Lala passes. The
threat for flooding increases over Maui County this evening and
spreads to the rest of the state later tonight through Sunday. Heavy
rainfall could persist into Monday for some areas, mainly over the
western end of the island chain. Lala is expected to produce
additional rainfall totals of 5 to 10 inches across the Big Island and
Maui County and 4 to 6 inches across the remainder of the island
chain. Locally higher amounts are possible. While the highest rainfall
amounts will be focused over windward areas and higher terrain,
leeward areas will also have a significant flood risk.

Sustained winds of 35 to 55 mph with gusts as high as 85 mph are being
observed for leeward Kohala and portions of West Maui this evening.
25 to 35 mph sustained winds with gusts of 40 to 60 mph are also
ongoing along the Saddle Road, as well as for Kau District and large
portions of Maui. Hurricane conditions, with sustained winds over
74 mph, remain possible across the Big Island. Tropical storm
conditions, with sustained winds over 39 mph, are expected for
portions of Maui County through Sunday morning and the western islands
through Sunday evening. It is very important to note that the
mountainous terrain of the islands will likely produce localized areas
of highly enhanced and damaging winds, even well away from the
tropical cyclone center.

East swell is beginning to subside for the Big Island but is currently
peaking for Maui County. Surf will continue to build further west,
peaking tonight for Oahu and tomorrow morning for Kauai. Some increase
in surf is also possible along exposed south- facing shores as Lala
continues westward. Significant beach erosion and overwash are still
possible across vulnerable coastal infrastructure.


POTENTIAL IMPACTS
-----------------

* WIND:
Potential impacts from the main wind event are now unfolding across
the Big Island of Hawaii and Maui. Remain well sheltered from
life-threatening wind having additional extensive impacts. If
realized, these impacts include:
- Considerable roof damage to sturdy buildings, with some having
window, door, and garage door failures leading to structural
damage. Mobile homes severely damaged, with some destroyed.
Damage accentuated by airborne projectiles. Locations may be
uninhabitable for weeks.
- Many large trees snapped or uprooted along with fences and
roadway signs blown over.
- Some roads impassable from large debris, and more within urban
or heavily wooded places. Several bridges, causeways, and
access routes impassable.
- Large areas with power and communications outages.

Potential impacts from the main wind event are also now unfolding
across the rest of the state. Remain well sheltered from dangerous
wind having additional limited to significant impacts.

* FLOODING RAIN:
Potential impacts from the flooding rain are still unfolding across
the Big Island of Hawaii and Maui. Remain well guarded against
life-threatening flood waters having additional extensive impacts. If
realized, these impacts include:
- Major rainfall flooding may prompt many evacuations and rescues.
- Rivers and tributaries may rapidly overflow their banks in
multiple places. Small streams, creeks, canals, arroyos, and
ditches may become dangerous rivers. In mountain areas,
destructive runoff may run quickly down valleys while
increasing susceptibility to rockslides and mudslides. Flood
control systems and barriers may become stressed.
- Flood waters can enter many structures within multiple
communities, some structures becoming uninhabitable or washed
away. Many places where flood waters may cover escape routes.
Streets and parking lots become rivers of moving water with
underpasses submerged. Driving conditions become dangerous.
Many road and bridge closures with some weakened or washed out.

Potential impacts from the flooding rain are still unfolding across

properties.areaDesc: Chuuk Coastal Waters
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued August 15 at 4:44PM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
properties.description:
An unsettled monsoon pattern, associated with Invest 92W continues
to intensify across eastern Micronesia. Invest 92W is currently rated
sub-low by the Joint Typhoon Warning Center, which means development
into a significant tropical cyclone is not expected at this time.
However, the latest ASCAT pass does show a low-level circulation
center with near gale winds to the south of Chuuk. This indicates at
least a bit of organization that could bump 92W up to low later
tonight or Sunday. Somewhat of a lull in showers and storms is
occurring due to changes in Invest 92Ws structure, and drier air
mixing into the storm. Conditions are expected to become more
favorable for development of the storm next week. Periods of locally
heavy showers and thunderstorms are expected through much of next
week. Gusty winds are expected near heavier showers.

Additional rainfall amounts of 5 to 10 inches are possible through
next week, with additional rainfall possible next weekend.
These rainfall amounts could result in flash flooding and
potential mudslides. Towards the latter half of next week, a monsoon
surge could develop and continue to impact Chuuk. Residents across
Chuuk State should monitor local forecasts and heed advice of
emergency managers when heavy rainfall occurs.

NWSheadline: A TROPICAL DISTURBANCE NEARBY BRINGS HEAVIER SHOWERS AND GUSTY WINDS THROUGH MUCH OF NEXT WEEK

to intensify across Pohnpei and Kosrae. Invest 92W is currently rated

middle of next week. These rainfall amounts could result in flooding
and potential mudslides. Residents of Kosrae and Pohnpei should
